cases.candidate_script:
H=/opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/dnssec-cname-chain-peer.py
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" prep || exit 98
export BASHDNS_TRUST_ANCHOR="$PWD/anchor.ds" BASHDNS_FIXTURE_DIR="$PWD/fixtures" BASHDNS_0X20=0
mkdir -p "$BASHDNS_FIXTURE_DIR"
name=a; for ((i=1;i<70;i++)); do name="$name.a"; done
/usr/bin/python3 - "$BASHDNS_FIXTURE_DIR" "$name" <<'PYEOF'
import pathlib,struct,sys
root,name=sys.argv[1:];q=b''.join(bytes((len(x),))+x.encode() for x in name.split('.'))+b'\0'+struct.pack('!HH',1,1)
(rootpath:=pathlib.Path(root)).mkdir(exist_ok=True)
(rootpath/(name+'.A.bin')).write_bytes(struct.pack('!HHHHHH',0x1234,0x8180,1,0,0,0)+q)
PYEOF
if dns query "$name" A -s 127.0.0.2 -t 1000 --validate > long.out 2> long.err; then echo depth=wrongly-accepted; exit 1; fi
if [[ $(<long.err) == *'chain too deep'* ]]; then echo depth=bounded; else echo depth=wrong-error; exit 1; fi
cases.purpose: Reject over-depth DNSSEC chain candidates before indexing fixed-size label arrays.
cases.oracle: An independently constructed syntactically valid 70-label DNS question reaches the chain-depth guard through the fixture path.
cases.comparison: Must report the explicit bounded-chain failure rather than accept, crash, or rely on a timeout.
